newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH EMU MEMBERSHIP GETS SUPPORT FROM TOP DAILY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH EMU MEMBERSHIP GETS SUPPORT FROM TOP DAILY.

text.p: Finland's biggest daily newapaper Helsingin Sanomat at the weekend said it supported Finnish efforts to join European economic and monetary union from its scheduled start-up on January 1, 1999.

It said Finland, whose government is anxious to be among the first wave of countries joining a single currency, should go ahead even if Sweden, its neighbour and key rival in the forest industry, does not.

"We should be involved regardless of what Sweden decides because, if the union succeeds, its benefits to us will be greater than its disadvantages and because the risks of delaying membership seem, in the end, to be bigger than those that joining would bring," the paper said in a leader on Sunday.
"As a member of monetary union, Finland can influence its success from the very beginning. Outside, we would simply have to adjust," Helsingin Sanomat said.
The paper said monetary stability and low inflation had become key goals regardless of the integration process.
It added that for Finland, political considerations of EMU were at least as important as economic ones.
"After the end of the cold war, Finland joined the EU to get a recognised place among Europe's western democracies and a vote in their joint consultations," the newspaper said.
"The monetary union is the next important stage in the EU's continuing process of integration," it said.

If the European Union were at some stage to be divided between a core and a looser group of member countries, then the dividing line would most certainly run between those countries that join the monetary bloc and those that stay out, it said.
"EMU is a necessary condition for the expansion of the EU, which Finland has committed itself to supporting, especially as far as the Baltic countries are concerned," it said.
